utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Mr. Registrar, would you please call case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, The Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Is the witness -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the witness is being brought in, if I could just address the Court on a housekeeping matter. Yesterday the transcripts were given one exhibit number which was P1150, but I have been advised that that could cause some problems because there are three sections of the transcript, and unlike the previous instances, the transcripts, these particular transcripts don't bear register assigned page numbers, so we have to go through the particular ERN number and the page number, and each section has its page numbering starting from afresh, which mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that every page reference would be a multiple choice question, is it one, two, or three.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Exactly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar is this ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Your Honours, we can assign individual exhibit numbers to each document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we describe them as the transcript, first part; transcript, second part; and transcript, third part. So that it is clear from the description that it consists of three parts. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Transcript, first part, 65 ter number 06161 will remain exhibit number P1150. The second transcript, 65 ter 06162, becomes exhibit number P1151. And the third transcript, 65 ter 06163, becomes exhibit number P1152.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. It follows from our decision yesterday that P1150, P1151, P1152 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkalj. Good morning. Please be seated. Mr. Turkalj, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne will now continue her examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now yesterday the last question I asked you was if you had rules of engagement in -- engaging in artillery operations, and your answer was that you didn't have rules of engagement but that you had -- that you used tactics of artillery based on which you acted upon during the operation. Now, did those tactics --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I don't believe that is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there is any dispute what the witness said, please literally quote him, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: The answer: "There were no rules of engagement for artillery per se. What we had in place was the tactics of artillery, based on which we acted upon in the course of the operation." This is at page 13556, line 22. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. My statement is that that in -- it envisions many different issues when it talks about artillery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, Ms. Mahindaratne has now put to the witness what he literally said, and that was the purpose of this exercise, not to start exploring the differences between the original and the later quote. Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now my question to you is, Mr. Turkalj, did those tactics include specifications which required you to maintain a minimum -- a prescribed minimum distance from civilian settlements in engaging targets or in the process of selection of targets?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can answer the question in the following way: There existed specific information about the location of the military targets, and to us, they were targets, as such.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Were you instructed by Mr. Markac, Mr. Sacic -- I'm sorry, the inner control branch or any authorities that engaging targets, whatever the targets that you had been provided with as those that you should consider in firing at or ordering attacks on, that you should take into consideration the distance between that target and civilian settlements or civilian structures?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to line of this questioning for this reason: It presupposed that Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic or the inner control have that specific authority to direct them to do that. So if she can establish that foundation, then the question is relevant. If not, then there's not foundation for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My questions was whether he ever received instructions, so as to whether this comes into the purview of Mr. Markac, Mr. Sacic, or the inner control branch is not my question. My question is a whether he has received. And it's a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's at least a question about facts. It's not for the first time that an issue arises whether orders, instructions were given, received, although there may be some doubt as to the authority to issue such orders, so therefore, it is appropriate to put questions of fact whether anything was received, whether any orders were given, any instructions given. The question about authority which, of course, is not -- is partly a question of fact can be the following question: Not necessarily such a clear, factual question should be preceded by first exploring the authority to do what the witness is asked whether that has been done. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you please answer my question, Mr. Turkalj, or do you wish me it repeat it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can answer your question. When we received information about the location of military targets and all the other related information that we thought was interesting in an offensive action, in an attack action, when we spoke to Mr. Sacic and two or three days earlier with Mr. Markac, we were told that when selecting targets we should pay attention to artillery fire, in order to make sure that the civilians, if any in the area, do not come in harm's way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when did Mr. Markac tell you -- tell that to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: This was probably a day before the start of Operation Storm. In a conversation we had.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now you said when we received information about the location of military targets and all the other related information. What were the other related information which was provided to you when you were provided with the -- with locations of military targets? What is the other relevant information?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: When I refer to information, I mean the information we had concerning the 9th Motorised Brigade which was positioned ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So that is what -- was there any other information such as how far the particular target was to a civilian settlement, how many civilians were present in the settlement, such information, was that given to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I believe that I answered this question yesterday. Based on the topographic map of the area, I was able to gauge the distances between the civilian features and military targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Turkalj, were you aware of the range of error for the artillery that you were using?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: For firing upon military targets, we used the most precise type of artillery pieces we had at the time. The range of error is from 12.5 to 25 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And for which weapon is that? What type of weapon are you giving that probable range of error?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I'm referring to 130-millimetre cannons and about calculating the elements for artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And for 120-millimetre mortars, what was your probable range of error?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: When calculating the elements involved, I believe the range is roughly the same. Range of error, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And you also use, in the course of the operation, MBRL, multi-barrel rocket launchers systems, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now your testimony is that you used -- you said for firing upon military targets, we used the most precise type of pieces we had at the time. What were the most precise pieces that you considered to be appropriate for you to be using in the course of the operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: [French on English channel]... 130-millimetre cannons for the targets that are deep -- the rear that are deep behind the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... get a translation for the answer, for most of the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you repeat the question, Ms. Mahindaratne, there are -- it doesn't appear on the -- on the transcript in full detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, we lost part of your answer. Let me repeat my question to you, if you could answer. Now, you -- what type of artillery pieces that you -- did you consider to be capable of firing with position? You said precise pieces. What exactly were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I said that the most precise artillery piece we had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, by way of clarification on these issues I looked at the statement that he gave, which is P1049, and I have, of course, have read P1150, 1151, and 1152, which are the three statements, and if counsel could point to me where this discussion ensues concerning the various uses of artillery, I would be illuminated. Because I read this, and while there is a brief discussion about artillery, there is certainly no discussion on there score. I just want to be looking in the right direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It my be a --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this -- this amount of detail has not been explored in the course of the interview, and as such, it is not in the statements nor in the interview transcripts. However, we have -- the Prosecution has not had the benefit of proofing this witness, or we have not had any communication with this witness. And I believe this witness has the knowledge and facts that the Trial Chamber would be interested in assessing the other evidence. I do not know on what basis I could be barred from proceeding with this line of questioning just because it has not been dealt with previously. If it is an issue of disclosure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, you may proceed this line of questioning. It is a follow-up, and a -- of one of the answers of the witness where he made precise -- he gave precise information, the 12.5 to 25 millimetres asked for further exploring. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could just on that score, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Kehoe, Ms. Mahindaratne may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I would like to discuss this at the break, Judge, because there is an issue of disclosure that I'd like to put on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The disclosure issue, that is something different. I do not know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a disclosure issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, when I referenced Your Honours to the several hundred page statement that Mr. Turkalj gave, P1150 through 1152 as well as prior it statement where the Office of the Prosecutor had numerous Russ sessions to discuss this with the witness, there is no discussion about margin of errors on T-130s or margins of errors on mortars.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is triggered about by the answer of the witness, Mr. Kehoe. If the witness would have said the precision is 10 centimetres to 20 centimetres, everyone would have would accepted that and if -- so therefore, that's the reason, as I explained, the disclosure issue, the line of questioning is accepted by the Chamber as a logical sequence of one of the answers given, where Ms. Mahindaratne did not ask -- asked about precision of weapons which is, in this context, quite logical. So therefore Ms. Mahindaratne is allowed to continue. I consulted my colleagues on this decision, which is a Chamber decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I note my objection to the record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, could you answer my question. Let me repeat it again. What weapons did you consider to be -- when you used the term, you said: I used precise -- or the most precise equipment. What were the weapons that you were referring to there?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I said that we used the most precise artillery pieces we had at our disposal at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what were they?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: We used 120 mortars, multi-barrel rockets and cannons. And cannons are among the most precise weapons. Also Howitzers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So you said you used multi-barrel rockets. Did you consider multi-barrel rockets to be a weapon capable of firing with precision?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No, that weaponry can fire with precision, but multiple barrel launchers are used to cover a surface and not a target which is a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you clarify that answer further. When you say a multi-barrel -- let me just read it back exactly. You said part of your answer has not been recorded. You said, It is used to cover a surface and not a target. Can you clarify that, bear with us, Mr. Turkalj. We are not very knowledgeable about artillery. So could you specifically, you know, tell us what you mean by that. Surface in what sense?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: In the military sense the multi-barrel rocket launcher is used to cover a target which is an area like a room. I don't mean a room in terms of a building. A room, in this strict sense, would mean an area of 100 by 100 metres, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what type of military targets would you used multi-barrel rocket launchers systems against, what type of target, what could you articulate? And going back to your testimony yesterday, you said when I asked you what type of targets were -- you provided you said, you provided with certain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, this is an area that there has been absolutely no disclosure. We're now asking for an expert opinion on a particular area, and the OTP, A, has certainly has not put him in the expert category; and, B, there is no disclosure in this line in any of these statements. None. This is a new line of questioning that Ms. Mahindaratne has decided on this morning with this witness. Now the accused is entitled to disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. In fact, this line of questioning is ensuing from the responses given by this witness. In fact, the witness yesterday testified as to what type of targets he was provided with, and this morning, he himself, offered that testimony about position weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not all at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If I could say, Mr. President, I'm not seeking an expert opinion. The witness was in charge of artillery, and I'm asking him -- this is factual matters. This is it not an expert opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Look at the last question that Ms. Mahindaratne asked, if that is a factual matter. So what type -- this is on line 6 of page 15: "What type of military targets would you use multi-barrel rocket launchers systems? What type of target? What could you articulate?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would change that question in relation to the targets that were given to you, what type of weapon you used, then it suddenly is not expert anymore, then it's just a question about facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... we could start analysing the way in which you formulate exactly the question where it is a question of fact and where it becomes a question of opinion. Let's not spend time on that. You have heard that by reformulating the question slightly it becomes well, let's say, for 95 per cent a factual question. You're invited to focus on facts.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will do so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: If I might add, as Your Honours knows, we have the statement and we have the three transcripts. And I don't know if Your Honours have read that or not. 99 per cent of what Mr. Turkalj says in those statements and transcripts has nothing to do with artillery. So it is, in all honesty, a disclosure issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he told in the statement what artillery was used, so therefore some follow-up questions in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I do agree with Your Honour, and there is no question that that did occur and that witness did talk in some small instances about that in his statement. But the focus of this examination isn't necessarily on what has been discussed in the transcripts or in the statement. It is on something almost entirely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You can argue how different and how close it is. Ms. Mahindaratne, there is it some merit in what Mr. Kuzmanovic says. There is certainly also merit in what Mr. Kehoe says about the formulation of the question and when he becomes an expert. But since you rely mainly on the, I would say, on the experience of the witness, you can ask him about his experience, and then it's not expert evidence, but it's experience. Just to give you an example. You didn't ask him any further questions on the 120-millimetre mortars. Now you can ask someone what exactly is the error range, et cetera he is you can also ask a witness, Did you fire mortars at -- with the different charges, did you ever notice a difference in position when you used a one charge or a six-charge. Then you ask for facts and matters the witness may have observed personally and which may have relevance for the issue here. Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the difficulty without going to specific facts is that the margin of error not only with cannons and Howitzers and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Kehoe, we are not going to discuss here the substance of what apparently is the disputed content of the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The only issue, Judge, is when the facts are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no. If you want to do that, we first to ask the witness whether he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can ask the witness to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, do you understand or speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your earphones for a second, please. Yes, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: On this issue, Your Honour, and the reason I was getting back to the facts and why the facts are important is because issues concerning margin of error et cetera and all this weaponry depends on distance, depends on weather conditions. A --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have fully agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On that matter it is not without reason that I said you can ask a witness whether he has fired mortars with one charge or six charges which, of course, also the angle makes quite a difference, and I think that with a be important for Ms. Mahindaratne to know. She said we're not expert ourselves in artillery. That putting a question about an error of -- margin of error doesn't make very much sense if you do not have other information available, such as weather conditions, atmosphere conditions, charges used, angle of firing, there are a lot of -- at the same time, Mr. Kehoe, that also explains why if a witness says, Well, I used this weaponry, and they have 12.5 to 25 meters of margin of error, and would that be true for the -- that is true for the cannons. Would it be true for the mortars as well? Yes, approximately the same. These, of course, are answers which justify further exploring on what exactly was taken into consideration when firing this type of weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I will say that -- that the facts are important, but the overall facts on non-disclosure virtually precludes from cross-examining on this because we had no notice that this was an area that going to be the subject of the Prosecution's direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Mahindaratne might not have been prepared for an answer of 12.5 to 25 metres as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: She asked the question what the margin of error was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but she may be surprised by the answer. That's why I gave that answer earlier. If you say -- if you put a general question to a witness and you receive an answer, which might come to some spent as a surprise, then even if you had not in mind to explore in detail such matters, that this might cause you to do so because of the unexpected answer. Let's -- Ms. Mahindaratne, you are aware that there is -- there are objections against putting this witness in a situation where he more or less serves as an expert witness on all kind of details, on margins of errors, technical details of weaponry. At the same time, I left you some margin to put some questions. If you would keep that in mind, that these objections, as I said before, are not totally without merit, although not sufficient at this moment to bar you from putting some questions in relation to this, but certainly not -- this is not a green light for exploring in every detail this area, which certainly does not prominently appear in the statement of the witness. If you would please keep that in mind, then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President. Thank you for those guidelines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, would you ... And may I urge the parties to see whether we can have a flow of evidence, which is not interrupted on a minute-by-minute basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I appreciate that. And to and to the extent I did that, personally, Your Honour, I apologise to the Chamber and to my co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, now you said -- and I'm just going back to what you just said with regard to 120-millimetre and 130-millimetre cannons, you said the probable range of error that you considered was 12.5 to 25 metres. Based on what did you arrive at that figure?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I arrived at that figure the following way: It includes all the elements that need to be put into the calculation when firing, stating that the margin of error could be as little as 12.5 metres. I know all that because I completed the Military Academy. I can add to that, that if one has a computer at one's disposal, if you do it electronically, then the calculation gets even more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you use -- in directing the artillery operations, did you use any charts or any written instructions that set out the margins of error, the -- the other elements that need to be factored in calculating the probable range of error with regard to particular types of weapons. Did you use such material?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I did not fully understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, within the special police artillery section, were there any specific instructions given with regard to are, let's say, example, that the probable range of error related to go 120-millimetre mortars would be such-and-such when -- when you factor in the particular charge you use, the particular elements of weather, so on and so forth, were there written instructions or certain charts that you used?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic, the question started as a factual question. When reformulating when the witness said he didn't understand the question. It might that be the question changed a bit of character. If would you not mind, Mr. Kuzmanovic, and if that would deal with the objection you may have, I could try to reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: My objection actually was in part that, Your Honour. But the main objection I have is the question assumes that the special police itself has an artillery section, and I think that needs to be established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps -- when you were -- Mr. Turkalj, when you were in charge of the use of artillery, do you know whether any tables were used to calculate what margin of error would apply in the specific circumstances of the use of that weapon; that is, calibre, angle of firing, charge, et cetera? Were you using tables? Were they available?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Specifically when determining the elements for firing of artillery weapons, there were tables. Each piece had its own respective table, and that is what we used to determine the elements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how specific were these tables? What elements appeared on this table resulting in a certain margin of error? How detailed were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The tables were precise, drafted by experts. We were not the authors of those tables. We merely used them. The tables do not originate from the special police. Those tables are used by armed forces all over the world. They have nothing to do with us, and the elements depend on the coordinates of the target, direction, distance, and all the other elements one needs to have in order to engage a target.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: You said, Mr. Turkalj, that these tables were used by armed forces all over the world. Now, the tables that you used, what were the origins of those tables? I mean, you could not have been using a universal table. What -- can you tell us from which military force or which armed forces had -- or from which authority had issued those tables?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: From the point of view of artillery, such tables depend on the piece you use. There were such tables in existence in the eastern part of the world and the western part of the world. The difference may have been between 60 and 64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, do you know generated these tables? Was it -- the ones you used, were they JNA table, were those American tables, were those manufacturer tables; do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were JNA tables, provided they corresponded with the pieces we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Turkalj. Now going back to your testimony yesterday, you said that you were provided with designated targets which included targets on the front lines, and then you also said that you were provided with certain targets in the depths behind the lines, which you describe as, and I will read them to you: Command points, railroad junctions, warehouses of equipment pieces, communication centre. And you said that would be it more or less. Now when I just asked you about the 128-millimetre multi-barrel rocket launcher systems and as to what type of targets you use such a weapon, you said for surface areas, not specific targets. Now did you, in the course of the operation, use multi-barrel rocket launchers systems against a type of weapons that you described yesterday? That is, the targets in the depth which were command points, railroad junctions, warehouses of equipment, or communication centres?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Multi-barrel rocket launchers were used exclusively to engage the enemy defence at the front lines and the rear, meaning up to one or two kilometres where the enemy forces are, just behind the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So if I could understand your answer, is it correct that you're saying that the multiple rocket launchers were used only against forces, that is personnel, by you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. The previous answer wasn't complete. In terms of what the witness said. I don't know if there was a gap in the translation or what happened, but the answer is not complete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, on the record, I, at this moment as your last answer: Multi-barrel rocket launchers were used exclusively -- I think you said for front line positions and positions in the rear, positions in the rear, meaning up to one or two kilometres where the enemy forces, just behind the front line, were. Is that -- because we are missing part on the transcript. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If could you clarify, did you mean that they were used only against forces, as in personnel?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, you said that -- previously you said that three days before the operation, Mr. Markac had informed you or had -- at a meeting had been told, you had been instructed to take care of -- take care that civilians would not be in harm's way in using artillery. Now, what type of steps did you take to ensure that, to minimise collateral damage?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: We took all the steps necessary. We designated the targets at the front line and in the rear of the front lines along the axis of attack of the special police. We also designated the targets within our area that were important for the fulfilment of our goal. We were precise in terms of what the goals were in the entire area. We prepared the axes of attack, and we had a battery covering each of those within their respective areas. The artillery we had had a longer range, and it was exclusively under my control. Therefore, no one could have acted without my consent.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So were there any designated targets involved in the course of the operation which were close to civilian settlements?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I'm afraid you will have to repeat your question. There were fortified targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Because the front line was being put in place for three years before the attack itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, one clarification, Mr. President. I apologise for the interruption. If counsel could designate in her question or describe what she means "close to civilian settlements," what that means in artillery respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, now, you referred to targets, designated targets, in the depths, and you described -- I referred to those four types of targets. Were there such targets located either within civilian settlements or, say, within proximity of 50 to 300 metres to civilian settlements or civilian structures?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I would seek further clarification. Are you talking about any targets in settlements or the targets along the axes of attack of the special police?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm referring to the targets in depth, not on the confrontation lines. You referred to four types of targets which were designated in the depth. Were there such targets located in villages or towns or near villages or towns? Let me be more specific. Which fell within the probable range of error as you saw it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Probable range of error is not a good -- you earlier said within 50 to 300 metres [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'll stick to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Could you answer that question, Mr. Turkalj. Did you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: If I understood your question correctly, the direction of attack of the special police was a bit wider in range than the territory we have been discussing so for at Mount Velebit. Along the axis of target there were many targets, not only the four or five that we referred to yesterday. Those targets as well as others were in proximity of certain settlements, some of which were settlements as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So what kind of steps did you take to ensure that collateral damage was minimised? Now you said that you had instructions to ensure that civilians would not be in harm's way. So my question to you is what kind of steps did you take to ensure that?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As far as my work goes, and the work of artillery, we had two or three targets inside settlements. We worked very precisely on those occasions with a very small number of projectiles, seeking only to neutralize that particular target.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what were those three targets, and where were they?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I'm talking about the brigade command, the 9th Gracac Brigade, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And where was that located?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: It was inside Gracac itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And what were the other two?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Next, there was a cross-roads in Gracac itself, the two main roads, then there was a police station housing some of the operational forces in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: When you say in the area, which area?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The area along the axis of attack. Those were active forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you tell me -- when you say "axis of attack," what specific location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, let me try to understand what we're doing. You're exploring the three targets, which were close to settlements or even within civilian settlements. Does it make any difference whether in the police station there were people from a large area or a small area? We're talking about the police station housing persons as a target. Does it matter whether they came from far, whether they had red hair. Whether -- isn't the focus on targeting this -- this object.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Can you tell me first, Mr. Turkalj, what weapons did you use on those three targets? What particular weapon did you use?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: We used only the 130-millimetre cannon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And you said that you used -- let me be precise. You said you used only a small number of projectiles. For example, how many rounds did you have to fire approximately to neutralize, let's say, the police station housing forces?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can't give you a precise answer to that question. It would probably take an expert who would be prepared to answer that. In my view, it would take three or four rounds to neutralize the station or to put it out of operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And are there reports of expenditure of ammunition or that particular, you know, with regard to that day's operations. Is there any report that would give, ammunition expenditure that you have tendered, submitted to inner control branch or any special police authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Ms. Mahindaratne please speak into her microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: There were reports on the expenditure of ammunition for the operation for the whole of Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, we are reaching the limits. I earlier said that some follow-up questions that arise in the statement are allowed. But if we go to specific targets, et cetera, at least you should have given notice where you were not in a position to -- to proof the witness, that you would explore further, although without any proofing, certain matters, such as specific targets used. Because there is no basis for that in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you really have reached the limits, which I although not in a very concrete way, set to you earlier. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I will move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Turkalj, I'd like you to look at your statement, and that is the section under tab 2. For the record it is V000-5303, page 117 to 119. For the record, it is P1150. This is what you say in your testimony, and I read it to you. This is towards the bottom of page 117. Asked the question: "I would assume that through intelligence, perhaps from the military, you would be aware of whether the enemy had, perhaps, military installations?" Then the next page you say, The intellegence, military intelligence, was gathering information. They were using the aircraft -- and you're referring to self-manned drones. And you say, All the information that regarded that data, we got from the inner control department, and so you within the artillery, would have had the coordinates of where those locations were. Page 119 you said, Personally had, was given one or two photographs of those locations. And did you target those as a matter of course before the operation or when the operation commenced, or did you just wait until you were called up to, shall we say, use artillery on these locations? Your answer is, When the attack started, only one location was targeted, and all the rest, the artillery was used based on request of the commanders. There were not many locations targeted, and I can only name that the repeater Celavac was one of the targets, and there was one enemy position that was also targeted. You're talking about the predetermined targets. And now my question to you is: Now where was that enemy artillery position located which you fired at, which you referred to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: There were artillery enemy positions. At the very beginning of the operation, we were targeting an enemy Howitzer battery.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question was, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: That position was close to Sveti Rok. It is a settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now you say that only that position and the Celovac repeater was targeted at the commencement in terms of predetermined targets, thereafter, it was on the basis of fire support which has been called for from the ground. Now why weren't the other targets fired at at the commencement? Was there no necessity to fire those targets?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Perhaps you didn't quite fully understand the text here, or perhaps the investigator didn't quite understand it. When the commencement of the attack was signalled and when an order was issued, we fired upon these targets: The Howitzer battery, the communication centre. These were the targets that had to be neutralized so that we would not have difficulties in our attack. As the units advanced from their starting positions, they came into combat contact with the enemies and asked for support each along their own respective axes. I don't know what time of day it was, but it could have happened some ten minutes or half an hour after the start of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... my question was: Now with regard to predetermined targets, you said at the commencement that only those two were targeted. Were there any other targets which were designated or identified as being required to be engaged at the commencement of the operation, or was it only those two? And I'm not talking about --

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. Many targets were designated, not only two. My conclusion was that these two targets had to be fired upon right after the signal for the commencement of the attack was given. Other targets were fired at once the attack was under way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday when I asked you as to whether there were lists of targets, your response was not very clear. You said there were designated targets. I'm going to ask you that question again. These predetermined targets, were there written lists that were provided to you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I think it's all one and the same thing. The targets were determined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is were they put on paper one after another. That makes a list and whether they were determined, you can determine a target without putting them on a list, and that's apparently the question. Did you receive lists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The targets were determined on the topographic map based on which the activities took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: My question -- you're still not answering my question, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Mahindaratne, I specifically asked whether they were on the list, and now the witness says they were indicated on a map, which I understand, but we could verify that, that there was no list, but that you found them on this map. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correctly understood. The targets were plotted into the map. I put them down. The -- designated, the several targets and the basic information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you said you did put them on the map. Did you get them dictated by someone and then you put them on the map, or did you receive several sheets on which they were indicated? How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as I said yesterday, there was information from our service about the targets on the ground and the enemy forces that were positioned along the axis of attack of the special police. According to the information we had from our members who were on the front line, that line had been determined well ahead. We selected the targets that we thought were needed. And when it came to the artillery fire that was supposed to be active deep behind the lines, I designated the targets based on information I received from my department which contained the targets that were instrumental for the successful outcome of our operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That still -- let me try it verify whether I understood your answer. Is it that you got information by bits and pieces and that you put them on the map and that during the operation itself you received information -- information which made you decide what targets you had already on the map to be engaged; or possibly also targets not yet on the map? I'm trying to understand what you're telling us.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: What I've just said is that we decided which targets we would engage, based on the information we had which told us where exactly the targets were. This was the front line and shorter and longer distances behind the front line. Your question had to do probably with the targets on the ground that emerged at a later stage as new ones, and if we detected such, then they would be engaged as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So where you said, You decided which targets you would engaged, based on the information we had, which told us where exactly the targets were, you are talking about targets of which you had received information already prior to the operation, which you plotted on a map? Is that how I should understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now before the operation started, did you discuss -- once you had already plotted those targets, did you discuss or report back to Mr. Markac or Mr. Sacic as to -- with regard to those targets, did you inform them what targets you were going to engage in the course of the operation and show them either the map or whatever information you had?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I will not be able to give you as precise an answer as I would wish to. But Mr. Markac believed that I would do the artillery part of the job very well, and he certainly did not have cause to check --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That's not my question. I did not ask about what Mr. Markac thought about you. My question was, did you discuss those targets?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, it was an introduction to the answer, the answer being, as far as I understood it, that Mr. Markac left it to you, and that there was no later check on the way in which you performed that task. Is that what your answer was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I said. Mr. Markac trusted that in view of my qualifications and the experience in the artillery field that I would do the job very well. He had no reason to doubt that. On the other hand, he knew, I will repeat, that we do the job well, and there was no need for him to check later on which targets exactly we engaged along our axis of attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, Mr. Turkalj. Now, you did refer yesterday to the HV artillery support that was added to the special police for the operation. Now, in the course of the operation, who called for fire support from the HV unit that was added to the special police?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I think that the previous answers spoke of that particular unit. That's why I'm not quite clear on your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, my question is this: There was HV -- that there was HV artillery support that was added to special police for the operation, and that is your testimony. Now, in the course of the operation, who called for their fire support? I'm not asking as to who really brought them in, but who called for the fire support? Was it you or -- who would contact the HV unit that was providing artillery support and ask them to fire to the particular designated target?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Nobody asked of them to engage a particular target. Rather, I issued orders to these artillery pieces as to which targets they would engage. The support could be asked by the commanders who led their forces along their respective axis of attack, if they came into contact with the enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So the support asked by the commanders, did it have to go through you, or could the commanders who were leading the attacks contact the artillery batteries or groups or the HV unit directly and call for fire support, or did they have to inform you, and then you would then divert that particular request to the particular artillery unit? How did it happen?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Commanders along their axis of attack had their own support. There was a battery that followed that axis of attack. I'm talking about the main and auxiliary axes of attack of the special police. Where it was necessary to fire from 130-millimetres cannons from that particular firing position, then they would seek that sort of support solely from me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, the HV unit you described, if you required the HV unit to get involved or provide you with fire support, was it you who had contact them, or could the commanders who were leading the axis of attack contact them directly? That is my main question, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I've answered that. If it was necessary to fire, for instance, from 130-millimetre cannons, then they could have asked me to have them open fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: If there was a requirement to engage the rocket artillery fire, I'm referring to the multi-rocket launchers system, could the commanders who were leading the axis of attacks ask for that directly, or did that request have to go via you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Every commander along his axis of attack had a multi-barrel rocket launcher, 120-millimetre, of the RAK type. With that sort of multi-barrel rocket launcher, he could receive that sort of support without my clearance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, if you needed to have the rocket launcher that was within the HV unit that was providing support for the special police operation, if you required engagement of that equipment who would call for that support from the HV unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I think we're mixing units here. As to whether or not the HV unit that was working with them had the multi-barrel rocket launchers or just a T-130.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: In fact, his testimony is clear that the HV artillery support did have a rocket. Let me refer to the particular transcript reference. Actually, I get back to you, since it is specifically mention in the transcript, but I don't want to waste time. In the meanwhile, I will ask another question, and I will get back to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now let me just take you through your testimony, Mr. Turkalj. If I could ask you to go to your transcript V000-5303, the section under tab 2, page 89. Have you found that page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, could you assist us --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since I have an opportunity only to open one Adobe, could you always say first, second, or third, so that -- or refer to 1150, 151, or 52 so that I can find my way through the --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It's section 1, Mr President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Page 89.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: That is, Mr. Turkalj, the section under tab 2, page 89. And let me read what I'm -- I want to take you to. You were asked this question: Okay. Bearing in mind artillery is quite an important task, did you have any, shall we say, forward spotters or something travelling with the special police as they advance so that they could give accurate positions for area targeting? Are you on the page, Mr. Turkalj? And then your answer is -- goes to page 90: No, the reconnaissance there were units that were advancing. Commanders of the units were the ones who were assessing the situation and, if necessary, requesting support. You say there were coded maps. I don't know if you're aware of that. And let me just keep -- when there, on page 90 you say: "Based on those coded maps in each square [indiscernible], it was easy to determine precise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: It was easy to determine precise elevation points and to give precise instructions where the artillery should be acting, if necessary. So your testimony is there were no forward observers. So in the absence of forward observers, who corrected the fire for you?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Let me answer this way: Along the axis of attack of the special police, it is true that the commanders of the units sought -- sought support from their battery, and they had all had a coded map based on which, they were able to pinpoint the exact location of a target. Specifically when they came into cat contact with the enemy and when they engaged in combat, based on the coded map, they would not exactly where they were and where the target was, and then they would ask for the support from their battery which would fire at the target. Of course they were able to adjust their fire, if it was closer, further away, to the left, or to the right. Let me just add, the artillery batteries were not able to have their own observers or spotters because the terrain would not allow for that, but the commanders of units or rather, the commanders of specific axes were also observers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Why didn't the terrain allow for forward observers?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I suppose you didn't see the area. It's a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So if you're talking about the topographic preventing forward observers, how would the battery crew be informed, that, in fact, their round has either contacted with the designated target or that there has been a firing error which requires correction, if there was no mechanism to report back to the firing crew?

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he said -- Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's wait. What Ms. Mahindaratne is asking you is how you received the information to fire a little bit more to the left or to the right or a little bit further or a little bit closer. How did you receive and from whom did you receive that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was exactly the same system as the one you used by the artillery scouts or spotters, that you mentioned. The commander who sought support was the one who would give feedback to the battery as to where to direct their fire. He was, in fact, the observers and that system -- and since the communication system functioned perfectly, there were no problems there. I can explain this to you. Had this involved a military scout, or rather a forward observer, the same exact system would apply.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Are you saying, Mr. Turkalj, that the commander acted as a forward spotter. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: The commander who was present along the axis of attack and who was in command over on that axis and his associates and colleagues who were in the -- there, were able to guide the fire and correct the fire, since they were in contact with the battery. They all had these coded maps, based on which they directed the artillery fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, I'm looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I notice I have already gone over the time. This is a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a good time for a break. Then we will have a break, Mr. Turkalj. We will resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, now, you mentioned three targets which were in Gracac, and your testimony was that you used only 130-millimetre cannons to neutralize them. Did you ever call for the multiple rocket artillery fire on Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. Multiple rocket fire was not used in relation to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, when you called for fire on Gracac, did you ask for that fire support from the HV unit that was providing artillery support to the special police operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Let me be more specific. I ordered the fire position to engage targets.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Did you order the HV unit that was providing artillery support to the special police operation to engage targets in Gracac. That's my question. I'm referring to that -- that HV unit that was added to the special police operation.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I don't know if we understand each other. When we're talking about 130-millimetre cannons, that's the platoon that belonged to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Okay. That's -- that was my question. Now, Mr. Registrar, may I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek some clarifications. You were asked whether you ever called for the multiple rocket artillery spire on Gracac. Your answer was: "No. Multiple rocket fire was not used in relation to Gracac." Now calling for the use of certain weaponry is not exactly the same as it being used. Did you intend to say, I never asked, or perhaps even ordered, multiple rocket artillery fire on Gracac; or did you say, Well, I may have asked for it, but it finally was not used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The multi-barrel rocket launcher was not used in the activities on Gracac. The fire from that rocket launcher was neither asked for, nor was it used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Now, the second question, it was not entirely clear. Do I understand that the use of the 130-millimetre cannon, that you gave the order to fire this weapon, which was in the weaponry of the HV unit that was added to this special police operation? Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's well understood. The two cannons that were active along the axis of attack of the special police, they fired upon my order and upon my request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. Registrar, if could I have D1095.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, you see a document, and I appreciate you may not be familiar with this document. This is a daily combat report issued by the commander of the Zadar Operational Group dated 4th August. And can you take a look at the document if you're not familiar with it. I'd particularly like to draw your attention to paragraph 4 of this document, where it reads: "The MUP Ministry of Interior special units were supported by 130-millimetre guns and 122-millimetres Howitzers in the first sector engaging Gracac and the area behind the lines. The support was weakened by the belated arrival of the SVLR, self propelled multi-barrel rocket launchers and ammunition," and then there is some further details. And then, "the entire day the artillery was engaging the front line and the area deep behind the enemy lines." Now, there is a reference here to the SVLR rocket arriving belatedly, and the support being weakened because of that. Did you at any time call the -- the HV unit which was providing you with artillery support to use the multiple rocket launcher on any targets?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: As far as this report is concerned, I didn't have an opportunity to see it, though this is my view of it. This is the information where the operations group Zadar or someone on behalf of that group is submitting a report that they were seven days late in arriving at their firing position. In other words, they were not present at the start.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to you is, did you ask the HV unit that was supporting artillery operations of the special police to provide multiple rocket fire on any targets in the special police axis of attack?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: Yes, we did ask for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: What were those targets that you asked for that fire against?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: To engage personnel.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: In the area at the foot of the Velebit, along the axis of the axis of attack of the special police, then in the area of Mount Velebit at the Prezid Pass. Those were the targets we worked on during the operation. There was several targets. Not just one.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, may have I document 1403, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you an another document, and you probably will be familiar with this document, Mr. Turkalj. This is the -- what is known as the war path, and this an extract of the war path, of the, pardon my pronunciation, Bjelovarsko-Bilogorska special police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if you could take to the English document page 6 and on the Croatian version page 5. And if we could focus on paragraph 3 of the -- page 6 on the English and the last paragraph on page 5 in the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now, in the English version around line 6 and the Croatian version the last paragraph about line -- last paragraph, I think about line 6, is that ... Mr. Registrar, I think we have the wrong ... are we on page 5 of the Croatian version? If we could go down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Mahindaratne, it seems to be chronological, so therefore one page back takes us back from the 6th of August, perhaps to the 4th.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just trying to find the point, Mr. President. I'm referring to that section in paragraph 3 of the English version which says: "On 6th August in accordance with the order of Turkalj."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I see at 0500 hours on the 4th of August. Is that what are you --

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No. Mr. Registrar, if you could about to the next page on the English version -- sorry, the Croatian version. Page 6 on the English version. On the Croatian version, if you could move to the next page. I'm sorry about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There we have the entry for the 6th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you note that paragraph that reads -- and on the English we are on the wrong page, Mr. Registrar. It's -- it should be page 6 on English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, what I see on my screen seems to be the right page, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, I see it is apparently ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Should be the previous page, page 6. Yes, this is the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Do you see that paragraph, Mr. Turkalj, which says: "On 6 August in according with the order of Mr. Josip Turkalj, the RTS was deployed in the region of Gracac, and around 2130 hours, part of the RTS of the Sisak-Moslavina police administration" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What you are reading now, does it that appear on your screen, and where does it appear on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 3, Mr. President, line 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, does it appear on the document on your screen, if you have the e-court?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the e-court Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But there are no line numbers or page numbers, are there?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I'm just trying to guide the parties where it starts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Tell me -- I have on my screen a document, to the left, English; to the right, Croatian. Could you tell us where in the English I find what you just read?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Paragraph -- third paragraph. I now see it, yes. In the middle of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Exactly. About five lines down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have found it, yes. And this does now also appear for the witness or the witness has a hard copy -- no, has no hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Now we are on the correct page, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, if you see the last paragraph, three lines from the bottom, it reads as follows: "On 6 August in accordance with the order of [Overlapping speakers] ... the RTS was deployed in the region of Gracac. And around 2130 hours, part of the RTS of Sisak Moslavina police administration's special police unit joined a part of Zadar police administration's special police unit." Now you just said that rocket artillery was not used on Gracac, and you did not ask for it nor was it used. Can you first tell us what is RTS?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I said that the rocket artillery was not used to engage Gracac. In this report, it says RTS, which is the rocket artillery group, and it is clear in the report that it was on my order that the RTS was deployed in the area of Gracac, meaning that they arrived at a position in -- in proximity of Gracac. On the 6th of August, the units had already passed Gracac. These people were following those units and, at that point in time, reached Gracac. They may have even spent the night there. They were billeted there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So your testimony is they were never ordered to fire on Gracac?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: No. They were billeted, accommodated there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Have I no objection, Judge, if the witness can just take his headphone off, I have just one comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you take off your headphones for a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has lead evidence -- I'm sorry -- in this report that Gracac had fallen by this point. I'm not clear on the line of questioning that the Prosecutor is engaged in, because at the time he is referring to that, the evidence that the Prosecution has put in already is that the special police had already taken Gracac, so I'm a little confused as to the relevance of this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I was merely seeking an explanation, Mr. President. We were wondering what it was, and the deployment of the RTS in Gracac, we were not quite clear what it was, and I thought this would be the witness to seek that explanation from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you wanted to exclude the possibility that there was any multiple rocket fired after Gracac had been taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I guess that is excludeing the possibility that the special police were firing on themselves given the evidence that the Prosecution is leading. But if that's the case, then we'll just move on. [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've heard the evidence. I take it that you move on to your next subject, Ms. Mahindaratne.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness -- could you put on your earphones again. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: May I call for document 1638, please. I'm sorry. It's 65 ter 1638. I'm sorry. I had not tendered the previous document into evidence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is why Mr. Kehoe has made an observation, but we have not heard from Mr. Kehoe if there is any objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number P1153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1153 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, can I have document 1638, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, this is a request from Mr. Markac requesting for logistic support from the HV Main Staff. And this is requesting for replenishment. Now are you able to say if, in fact, the quantity of ammunition which was being requested corresponds to the expenditure, daily expenditure, of the ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, just some clarity on that. Is he talking about the artillery level of the T-130s or the artillery that was deployed back down to the individual commanders in support of advancing troops?

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: I think it is a straightforward question, Mr. President, as to whether request for replenishment corresponds to expenditure. And I was particularly going to draw his attention to the 120-millimetre mortars and the 128-millimetre rocket fire -- rocket missiles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's hear the answer of the witness. Could you answer the question, Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As regards the replenishment with ammunition, we see items 1 and 2 that refer to artillery, these being the 120-millimetre mines and -- or and 128-millimetre missiles. Add regards the expenditure of ammunition, this could refer to the first day of operation. It was the logistics department that kept track of expenditure, and they were aware of their supply in the warehouses and what would be the amount required for the purpose of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: So being the person in charge of artillery, would you be able to say as to whether -- do you agree that, in fact -- or an amount close to 400 pieces of 128-millimetre rockets were used on the first day of operation by the special police artillery operations?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I would like to be able to precisely answer, but I can't know how much ammunition was spent the first day. As for the 400 pieces of 128-millimetre missiles, that could be possible for the first day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes exhibit number P1154.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P1154 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Mr. Turkalj, I'd like to you look at your transcript, 5304.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And for the benefit of -- it's section 2, P1051, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: And if you could look at page 14, you refer to Zeljko Sacic, the chief of special police, issuing you orders in relation to the artillery commitments for the advancement Donji Lapac, and you go on to say, Sacic was issuing orders, specifically all of us received our orders from him. And if you go on to page 15: "We also were given new maps because I personally did not have any map that would present anything further than Gracac, so we were given new maps there for that other area." Now, talk being maps, first question I want to ask you, you referred to previously also coded maps and your operations being conducted on the basis of maps. Were those maps preserved after the operation?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether there are still topographic maps in existence that were used during the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
utterances.text: Generally what did you do after the operation with regard to those maps? Were they handed over to a department in the special police, such as the inner control branch?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP TURKALJ
utterances.text: I want to go back to the part of the report, whereby it says that new maps were made upon entering Gracac and the headquarters was set up, the employees of the internal control department were then, at that point, working on a new map, a new topographic map, that could be used in the continuation of the operation. These were working maps, to be used by commanders to be able to navigate along the axis of attack and direction. As for artillery, it was useful for us to designate the targets which had already been plotted in and to designate any potential new ones. The system, the artillery functioned, remained the same as the one that was in place during the first couple of days of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MAHINDARATNE
